option_relations.rationale: Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) with cervical osteophyte-induced dysphagia is a distinct diagnosis and not related to Squamous cell carcinoma.
Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) with hypoglossal nerve palsy is a distinct diagnosis and not related to Squamous cell carcinoma.
Cervical osteophyte-induced dysphagia (Forestier’s disease) is a distinct diagnosis and not related to Squamous cell carcinoma.
Degenerative cervical spine disease is a broad category of conditions affecting the spine and is not directly related to Squamous cell carcinoma.
